html:
Bahla Fort is a huge mud-brick fortress in the oasis of Bahla in inner Oman, built mostly from the 12th to the 15th century by the Banu Nebhan, who ruled the interior then.

The oasis around it is ringed by a mud wall some 12 kilometres long and watered by aflaj. Bahla was famed for its pottery and, in folklore, for its jinn.

The fort was in ruins when it became a World Heritage Site in 1987 and was placed on the endangered list. It was restored over many years and reopened. With Nizwa and the Ibadi towns nearby, it shows the inland, oasis side of Oman.
sum: Bahla Fort is a huge mud-brick fortress in the oasis of Bahla in inner Oman, built mostly from the 12th to the 15th century by the Banu Nebhan, who ruled the interior then.
